title: Train the Agent, Not the Expert: Learning to Harness Heterogeneous Experts for Multi-Turn Visual Reasoning
claim: An agent reasons over multiple turns, calling a suite of specialized experts and archiving visual memory to solve complex tasks.
layout: 3 columns, left-to-right loop, labeled arrows Start/Parse/Return/End, prompt to final result
description: A three-column system diagram. On the left, a Prompt box holds a crowded aerial photo of dragon dancers with the query 'Detect/Segment/Count person dragon dancing'. Below it is the annotated final result, with a zoomed red inset and colored boxes. In the center, the Agent Reasoning panel has blue rounded boxes for Round 1 and Round 2, showing think text and tool_call JSON. Under it, the Dynamic Visual Memory Archiving panel has peach rows for Rounds 1 to 3, with image thumbnails and red notes that images will be replaced by text placeholders. On the right, the Environment panel shows an icon grid of the Heterogeneous Visual Expert Suite, a Controller, cache, selected worker, and an Expert Worker Pool. Yellow arrows labeled Start, Parse, Return, End and Agent Loop link the panels. Panel (a), the traditional specialists, is missing.
caption: From expert training to expert harnessing. (a): Traditional vision methods train a separate specialist for each sub-task. (b): VisHarness learns a harnessing policy over a set of heterogeneous experts and thus can solve complex visual tasks through multi-turn interaction.
abstract: Recent advances in computer vision have produced powerful specialized models for detection, segmentation, counting, and other visual tasks. However, these models are typically optimized for isolated tasks, limiting their ability to support general-purpose visual intelligence, particularly when complex language understanding and dense small-object perception are required. We propose VisHarness, a trainable visual agent that decouples high-level perception, reasoning, and decision-making from low-level task execution. Rather than training a task-specific model, we train VisHarness to harness a set of carefully designed heterogeneous visual experts. This paradigm preserves the agent's general intelligence while leveraging the precision of specialized visual experts for specific tasks. With only lightweight training, VisHarness learns a generalizable policy for harnessing visual experts, enabling it to solve fundamental vision tasks in diverse complex scenarios through multi-turn interactions with these experts. To enable efficient on-policy reinforcement learning in a live environment, we introduce dynamic visual memory archiving to reduce the visual-token overhead that rapidly accumulates during multi-turn interactions with visual experts. Experiments on four representative benchmarks spanning reasoning segmentation, generalized referring expression segmentation, dense small-object detection, and referring expression counting show that VisHarness substantially outperforms existing general-purpose models and is competitive with or superior to task-specific models. Our code, model weights, and training data are publicly available at https://github.com/fyw1999/VisHarness.
